draft.title: Making forecasts from trends
card: A trend is the general direction data moves over time, such as rising, falling or staying steady. On a line graph, it shows as the overall slope of the line.
To make a forecast, extend the trend past the last data point and read off the likely value. This is a prediction of what may happen next, not a certain fact.
A forecast assumes that the pattern continues. If conditions change, such as new laws, a disaster or a shift in people's choices, the trend can change too.
The more data points a trend is based on, and the shorter the distance it is extended, the more confidence a geographer can place in the forecast.
draft.remember: A forecast extends a trend to say what may happen next, but changed conditions can change the result.

a.q: A line graph shows a town's population rising steadily each year from 2010 to 2024. What does extending this line to 2030 give a geographer?
opts: A prediction of the likely population if the trend holds
The exact population the town will have in 2030
A record of the population in each year before 2010
Proof that nothing can change the town's population
a.why: Extending a trend gives a likely value based on the pattern so far. It is a prediction, not a certain fact, so it is not exact. The other options claim too much or look backwards.
a.clue: Extending a line says what may happen, not what will.

b.q: A council forecasts that its coastal suburb will keep growing at the same rate for 20 years. Then a new law stops any more housing being built there. What is the best conclusion about the forecast?
opts: It may now be wrong, because conditions changed
It is still certain, because the past trend was steady
It was wrong from the start, because forecasts are useless
It is better now, because the trend has more data
b.why: A forecast assumes the pattern will continue. A new law changes the conditions, so the trend may no longer hold and the forecast may be wrong. It was still a reasonable prediction when it was made, so forecasts are not useless.
b.clue: Ask whether the pattern can still continue after the law.

a.best: A prediction of the likely population if the trend holds

b.best: It may now be wrong, because conditions changed

problems.detail: The right option is the longest and the only one with a hedging qualifier ('likely', 'if the trend holds'), while the distractors make absolute or backward-looking claims, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
The right option is the only one with a hedge ('may'), while every distractor is absolute ('useless', 'certain', 'better'), so the answer stands out without knowing the idea.

proposal.remember: A forecast extends a trend to say what may happen next, but changed conditions can change the result.

a.q: A geographer extends a line graph of a town's population from 2024 to 2030. What does this forecast assume?
opts: That the pattern so far will continue
That conditions will change after 2024
That the trend will reverse after 2024
That the data before 2024 was wrong
a.why: Extending a trend only works if the pattern so far carries on, so a forecast assumes it continues. Changed conditions are the risk to a forecast, not what it assumes, because a change can break the trend.
a.clue: What must stay the same for the extended line to be right?

b.q: A council forecasts that its coastal suburb will keep growing at the same rate for 20 years. Then a new law stops any more housing being built there. What should the council do with the forecast?
opts: Review it, because conditions have changed
Keep it as it is, because the past trend was steady
Extend it to 40 years, because the trend is so steady
Throw it out, because forecasts are never useful
b.why: A forecast assumes the pattern continues. The new law changes the conditions, so the growth trend may not hold and the forecast should be reviewed. Keeping it because the past was steady ignores that changed conditions can change a trend.
b.clue: Can the old pattern still carry on after the law?

a.best: That the pattern so far will continue

b.best: Review it, because conditions have changed
